page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor running at 2.6 GHz. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate a performance profile that leans toward the lower tiers for intensive tasks. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance scores fall into the bottom 10 percent, with values of 767.9 and 1535.77 respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show weak performance in the bottom 25 percent, with read-only large block speeds at 31.36 GB/sec and write large block speeds at 16.16 GB/sec. However, the instance achieves average performance in specific workloads, such as single-threaded gzip compression at 23.96 GB/sec, single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 9.24 GB/sec, and Geekbench single-core execution with a score of 1305.0.

The ecs.c6a.xlarge presents a clear tradeoff between dedicated compute allocation and overall processing throughput. While it features dedicated AMD EPYC cores, its multi-threaded capabilities and database operations are relatively weak, as evidenced by a Passmark database score of 1356.62 and a Redis SET throughput of 3.57 million operations per second. This instance is best suited for lightweight compute tasks, basic web serving, text processing, and single-threaded utility scripts that do not require high memory density or local storage.

With a Passmark database score of 1356.62 and Redis throughput of 3.57 million operations per second, this instance is best suited for lightweight compute tasks, basic web serving, and single-threaded utility workloads.
